notes: SCOPE & METHOD: Covers all publicly known Apple acquisitions Jan 2020 – Aug 16 2026. Apple almost never discloses prices; every valueMillions figure is press-reported (source cited per deal), not Apple-confirmed — treat as 'reported'. Undisclosed = null. No divestitures: Apple made no material divestitures in this period. Many 2024–2026 deals only became public because Apple, as an EU Digital Markets Act 'gatekeeper' (designated Sep 2023), must notify acquisitions to the European Commission, which publishes summaries ~4 months later — hence closeDates sourced to 'EU DMA filing' are authoritative close dates. Total count here: 36 deals (11 in 2020, 2 in 2021, 2 in 2022, 3 in 2023, 4 in 2024, 8 in 2025, 6 in 2026 YTD). Edge cases: Camerai deal actually occurred ~2019 but was revealed Aug 2020 (listed 2020, closeDate null); Datakalab signed Dec 17 2023, revealed Apr 2024 (listed 2024 per revelation, closeDate 2023-12); Pixelmator announced Nov 1 2024, closed Feb 11 2025 (listed 2024 = announcement year, closeDate = actual close); TrueMeeting was reported by Bloomberg in 2024 but Apple's EU filing records close Jan 24 2025 (listed 2025); invrs.io is thinly sourced (MacRumors guide only). (a) PENDING-DEAL CARD: As of Aug 16 2026 there is NO officially announced, pending (announced-but-unclosed) Apple acquisition — searches found none. Best 'pipeline' item for a card: The Information reported Jul 15 2026 (via MacRumors https://www.macrumors.com/2026/07/15/apple-looking-to-acquire-ai-chip-companies/ and AppleInsider) that Apple is actively pursuing acquisitions of AI-chip companies to cut Nvidia dependence and is now 'prepared to do deals in the billions of dollars' — no named target, no announce/close dates or value, so it is exploratory interest, not a pending deal; label any card accordingly. Context: hardware chief John Ternus is set to succeed Tim Cook as CEO in Sep 2026, and reporting frames larger AI M&A as continuing under him. (b) TIM COOK ACQUISITION-PACE STATEMENTS: (1) Feb 23 2021, Apple annual shareholder meeting — Cook said Apple had acquired ~100 companies over the prior 6 years, averaging roughly one every 3–4 weeks, mostly for technology and talent (source: CNBC https://www.cnbc.com/2021/02/23/apple-shareholders-meeting-2021-approve-tim-cook-pay.html; MacRumors recap https://www.macrumors.com/2021/02/23/apple-2021-shareholders-meeting-recap/). (2) Jul 31 2025, Q3 FY2025 earnings call — Cook said Apple had acquired ~7 companies so far in 2025 and: 'We're very open to M&A that accelerates our roadmap. We are not stuck on a certain size company, although the ones that we have acquired thus far this year are small in nature' (source: earnings-call coverage, e.g. https://techstartups.com/2025/08/04/apple-quietly-acquires-7-startups-eyes-more-ai-acquisitions-as-investment-ramps-up/; CNBC). (3) For context, Q.ai (~$2B, Jan 2026) is Apple's second-largest acquisition ever after Beats ($3.0B, 2014) and largest since Intel's smartphone-modem business ($1.0B, 2019) — per MacRumors Jul 29 2026. Value discrepancy on Q.ai: US outlets 'close to $2B'; Israeli press $1.5–1.6B; dashboard should show '~$2B (reported)'.
